belief: I must figure out the reason for everything bad that happens.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that you must figure out the reason for everything bad that happens, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: A need for control and certainty. Anxiety that searches for answers to feel safe. Teaching that every event has a clear, knowable purpose. Painful events that seem senseless. Feeling that you cannot move on until you understand.
teaches: God has purposes in all things, but He does not always reveal them to us. The secret things belong to the LORD, while the things revealed belong to us. Even the wise cannot comprehend all of God’s work under the sun. Jesus told Peter, “You do not realize now what I am doing, but later you will understand.” Like a weaned child resting with its mother, we can quiet our souls before God without needing every answer.
self_statements: I can’t rest until I know why this happened.
There must be a reason, and I have to find it.
If I understood, I could accept it.
Not knowing means God doesn’t care.
I keep replaying it looking for answers.
Other people seem to understand their suffering.
errors: Needing to understand everything before you can have peace.
Going over events again and again looking for answers.
Assuming you can know God’s specific reasons.
Trying to manage pain by figuring it out.
questions: What does Deuteronomy 29:29 say about secret things?
Can even the wise understand all of God’s work?
What did Jesus tell Peter about understanding later?
Has searching for reasons brought me peace or more anxiety?
Can I trust God without knowing why?
What does it mean to quiet my soul like a weaned child?
What has God revealed that I can act on today?
truth: I do not have to figure out the reason for everything bad that happens. Some things belong to God alone. I may understand later, or not in this life. I can quiet my soul before God, trust His character, and focus on what He has revealed and what I can do today.
hw_questions: Can even the wise understand all of God’s work?
What did Jesus say about understanding later?
Has searching brought peace or anxiety?
Can I trust God without knowing why?
What can I act on today?
hw_truths: The secret things belong to God.
I can trust God without knowing why.
I may understand later, or not in this life.
I can quiet my soul before God.
God’s ways are higher than mine.
I can focus on what God has revealed.
log: When I start searching for “why,” write the question, then write: “This belongs to God,” and one thing I can do today.
name_example: Surely Sarah has stilled and quieted her soul; like a weaned child with her mother, like a weaned child is her soul within her.
actions: for questions about why; outside that time, gently set them aside.

tracker: One time I let a “why” rest
prayer: Father, You know the questions I carry. Help me reject the lie that I must figure out the reason for everything bad that happens. Teach me to quiet my soul before You, to trust You with the secret things, and to walk faithfully in what You have shown me. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
